Dubai's
thermal paradox.

The city that can look cooler by day—and retain heat long after sunset.

A source-grounded, reproducible exploration of urban heat in Dubai, and what it means for choosing effective interventions. Published measurements are kept separate from LUNARIS's own analysis and design scenarios.

01 / WHAT RESEARCH FOUND

Heat depends on when.

Peer-reviewed Dubai urban-heat analysis of 2022–2024 remote-sensing datasets. These numbers are the original researchers' results, not LUNARIS measurements or predicted benefits.

DAY / REGIONAL UHI CONTRAST−0.4°C

Mean daytime *urban cool island* effect reported by the study; not a universal temperature for every neighborhood.

NIGHT / SELECT VULNERABLE ZONES+5°C

Nighttime heat retention reported in the most vulnerable zones; not a typical Dubai-wide nighttime temperature.

LEADING MODEL FEATURE62%

Reported Random Forest feature importance for surface albedo within the study, not an intervention's effectiveness.

RESEARCH SOURCETesfaldet et al., Sustainable Cities and Society (2026), DOI 10.1016/j.scs.2026.107762 ↗

Authors assessed local climate zones and daytime/nighttime remote sensing using MODIS, Landsat and Sentinel-2. Underlying full study data are available from the authors on request; LUNARIS has not independently reproduced their LCZ findings.

02 / THE DESIGN QUESTION

What should a city investigate first?

01

Diagnose the time of exposure

Separate daytime walking-route shade from nighttime accumulated urban heat. A single daytime map is insufficient to rank both problems.

02

Identify the relevant surface

Study albedo, street shape, vegetation, shading, humidity and pedestrian routes. Different measures address different mechanisms.

03

Validate the site

Use measured temperatures, field access, permissions, water demand and maintenance constraints before calling a particular location a priority.

The selected Dubai Marina pedestrian corridor is a research illustration based on an approximate neighborhood anchor in LUNARIS Action. It has not been established as a thermal hotspot by this study.

04 / REPRODUCIBLE DATA ANALYSIS

Inspect the atmosphere.

NASA POWER offers daily 2 m air-temperature estimates. These characterize broader atmospheric conditions near the Dubai reference point, not street-scale satellite land-surface temperatures. They cannot alone confirm the paper's urban heat-island contrast.

NASA POWER POINT ANALYSIS

Data snapshot not bundled

Run the included Python script with internet access to download 2024–2025 daily observations, calculate descriptive statistics, and evaluate simple 2025 hold-out baselines. This page only displays measurements once the real output file is produced.

No fabricated observations or model scores.

DOWNLOAD / REPRODUCE

One command. Same dates.

python research/dubai_heat_case.py --output dist/app/action-atlas/dubai-heat-case/nasa_power_metrics.json

Run from the project root. Python standard library only. It also writes the full, dated daily source records to a companion JSON and validates completeness.

WHAT WE COMPARE

Baseline, not invented AI

For the 2025 unseen period, compare a prior-day temperature estimate with a 2024 calendar-day reference. Both have measured absolute error only if the NASA data download succeeds. These are simple baselines, not a trained LUNARIS ML model.
